note: #109: String#strip was Lean's `String.trimAscii`, which trims only space, \t, \n and \r, so NUL, \v and \f stayed attached ("\0a\0".strip was "\0a\0", "\v".strip was not empty). CRuby strips " \t\n\v\f\r\0" and nothing else, so the program sweeps all 256 bytes at each end and pins the exact set, then checks interior NULs, the C1 controls, Unicode whitespace, binary strings with a high byte, and the encoding tag. Exact program agrees with CRuby 4.0.5.
